title.justification: The title is clearly mentioned at the beginning of the paper.

analysis.description: The paper discusses a novel approach to asynchronous computation in graph neural networks (GNNs) by explicitly separating the concepts of node state update and message function invocation. This separation leads to practical implementations of scalable GNN layers invariant under various forms of asynchrony.

type.justification: The paper focuses on mathematical formulations and theoretical analysis to reason about asynchronous computation in algorithms and neural networks.
type.quote: With this separation, we obtain a mathematical formulation that allows us to reason about asynchronous computation in both algorithms and neural networks.

name.justification: The paper primarily discusses concepts and implementations related to Graph Neural Networks (GNNs).
name.quote: Message passing is the core primitive in graph neural networks [3, GNNs], a prominent family of deep learning models.

name.justification: The paper discusses neural algorithmic reasoning, which seeks to design neural network architectures that capture classical computation.
name.quote: Another active area of research for GNNs is neural algorithmic reasoning [13, NAR].

name.justification: The paper discusses PathGNN as an example architecture that aligns with the asynchronous computation framework proposed.
name.quote: This view allows us to study message passing under various synchronisation regimes—indeed, it allows us to theoretically justify the unreasonable effectiveness of architectures such as PathGNNs.

is_contributed.justification: PathGNN is used as an example and not introduced as a novel contribution within this paper.
is_contributed.quote: We refer to our new framework as asynchronous algorithmic alignment... it allows us to theoretically justify the unreasonable effectiveness of architectures such as PathGNNs.

is_executed.justification: The paper does not mention implementing or executing PathGNN; it is used as a theoretical example.
is_executed.quote: Note that we do not aim to implement an asynchronous GNN—a feat concurrently explored by AMP [18] and Co-GNN [19]—rather, we seek to build synchronous GNNs that are invariant—i.e., will yield identical output node embeddings—under various forms of asynchronous execution.

is_compared.justification: PathGNN is compared theoretically to the framework proposed in the paper.
is_compared.quote: This view allows us to study message passing under various synchronisation regimes—indeed, it allows us to theoretically justify the unreasonable effectiveness of architectures such as PathGNNs.
